name: exomemory
description: Let your assistant draw on your messages, notes and voice memos across platforms: past decisions, recommendations and ideas, with dated excerpts and source links.

interface.longDescription:
Exomemory lets ChatGPT draw on your life context and history: past messages, ideas and decisions from your WhatsApp, Messenger, iMessage and Telegram chats, your Obsidian, Notion and Apple Notes, and your voice memos. With that background it can work like an executive assistant who has been with you for years: brief you before a meeting, build a timeline of how something came about, or find who recommended what and when. Ask by topic, person or date, without worrying about exact wording, and let ChatGPT sift through the records, find what is relevant and quote it with dates and links to the originals.

You keep your data in your own hands: the archive lives on your computer. Exomemory connects ChatGPT to it through a relay that forwards each question to your computer and the answer back without storing either. Alternatively, assistants that run on your computer, such as Codex, can connect to your Exomem directly as a custom MCP server, without the relay.

Until you set up your own Exomem, the app shows a demo workspace with synthetic memories. The setup guide walks you through installing Exomem and adding your messages, notes and voice memos.

The tools are read-only, except when you choose to send optional feedback about the service itself.
defaultPrompt: I'm planning the Porto trip with Maya. Brief me on what we've agreed so far.
Build a timeline of the key decisions on Project Kestrel, with links to the original notes.
Find the voice memo where I explained why I changed my sourdough recipe.

positive.description: Answer a trip question from chats and notes
positive.prompt: What did we end up deciding for the Lisbon trip: the dates, where we stayed and which flight we took?
positive.expected_behavior: Searches the archive and answers from the Lisbon note and the group chat: 10 to 14 April 2026, a flat in Príncipe Real, and the SAS 11:40 flight from Copenhagen rather than the 07:05 TAP option. Cites dated excerpts and states that the results come from the synthetic demo workspace.

positive.description: Combine a note, a voice memo and a chat
positive.prompt: What hydration do I use for sourdough now, and why did I change it?
positive.expected_behavior: Answers that the house recipe since April 2026 is 75% hydration with 10% whole wheat, because the 80% loaves kept spreading flat in the oven. Cites the sourdough log with dates, and may also cite the 2 April 2026 voice memo and the chat with Priya.

positive.description: Find a person and summarise shared history
positive.prompt: Who is Priya Natarajan, and what have we talked about this spring?
positive.expected_behavior: Identifies Priya as a friend from the book club, which she organises from London. Summarises the Walden discussion, the next pick (The Overstory), the Lisbon trip and the sourdough starter she asked for at the end of April 2026, each with a date and source.

positive.prompt: List the decisions we made on Project Kestrel, with their dates.
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the decisions from the Project Kestrel note in date order: 19 January 2026 move from the nightly import to a Postgres-backed event queue; 11 February idempotent retries through a unique event id; 2 March launch on 22 April with a feature freeze on 1 April; 20 April a dead letter queue alert and an event-age indicator. May add the 28 April retrospective action and that it went live on 22 April 2026.

positive.description: Explain the service and the demo workspace
positive.prompt: What is Exomemory, and how would I set it up with my own chats and notes?
positive.expected_behavior: Explains that Exomemory connects ChatGPT to Exomem, a personal memory archive that runs on the user's own computer and is reached through exomem.io, that this connection currently shows a demo workspace with synthetic memories, and points to https://exomem.io/setup for installing it and importing exports. Does not present demo memories as the user's own data.

negative.prompt: Delete my notes about the Lisbon trip.
negative.expected_behavior: Explains that Exomem's tools only read the archive and cannot delete anything; the notes would have to be removed in the original app and re-imported. Does not claim that anything was deleted from Exomem. ChatGPT may separately update its own memory or preferences; that is a ChatGPT feature, not an Exomem tool.

negative.description: Nothing in the archive for the asked period
negative.prompt: What did Maya send me on WhatsApp yesterday?
negative.expected_behavior: Looks in the WhatsApp chats and reports that Maya sent nothing yesterday: the demo workspace's WhatsApp history ends in July 2026. May mention her latest WhatsApp messages (the Porto planning group) with their dates. Does not invent messages.

negative.description: Live information unrelated to personal memory
negative.prompt: What's the weather going to be in Lisbon this weekend?
negative.expected_behavior: Does not search the archive, since Exomem holds personal records rather than live data (it may first check what Exomem offers with capabilities); answers from other available means or says it cannot check the forecast.

publication.release_notes: First release. ChatGPT can search your self-hosted Exomem archive of messages, notes and voice memos by meaning, person, source or date; open any record with the conversation around it; follow links between notes; look up the people in it; and browse sources and collections. Answers come with dated excerpts and source links.
